predecessorSearch.preserveAndImprove: Preserve the underlying security question and practical publication risk. Replace the rejected technical-first opening, undefined API/reasoning terms, incomplete reader action and false show-your-work check with an audience-first explanation, visible mechanism, exact evidence limits and a purpose-built-report action.

examplePair.workplaceExample: A coding assistant reads a deployment key while diagnosing a website, omits it from the final answer and leaves a representation in the raw technical session a developer is considering publishing.
examplePair.nonWorkExample: A home-made travel assistant uses connected email and booking data; its owner shares the chosen itinerary rather than the raw technical export.
examplePair.sharedMechanism: The visible answer and the raw technical record are different layers; only a purpose-built share file limits the release to reviewed fields.
examplePair.surfaceAdaptation: The work case proves the paper's direct risk; the travel case transfers the same record-versus-result distinction without pretending an ordinary consumer chat was breached.

readerContract.humanQuestion: If I use an AI assistant, can private information hide in a file after the visible conversation looks clean, and what do I need to do?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader can distinguish ordinary chat from a raw technical AI-session file, explain how hidden continuity data travels and choose a safe share action.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: She knows what a chat and a file are; she is not expected to know what an API, reasoning block, signature or agent trajectory is.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: An AI application can receive a readable answer and a second opaque continuity item; cleaning the first does not sanitize the second.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: People share AI results at work and at home; the safe object is the checked result or a new allowlisted report, not the backstage technical session.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A dated plain-language Daily explainer of a newly published security study, with no false Breaking urgency.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I understand who this affects, why the finding matters, why I do not need to panic and exactly what I should share instead.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any paper correction, provider statement, new reproduction evidence or material change to provider reasoning/signature handling.

strengthsToUse: State the dated event and audience boundary.

patternsNotToCopy: Do not copy the legal-news structure.

Do not inherit the older story's scope, dates or public status.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: A new preprint found secrets in raw technical AI-session files outside the visible chat; the exact attacks stopped working after disclosure, and ordinary private chat use was not shown to publish a conversation.
causalSequence: An AI application receives a visible answer plus opaque continuity data.
During the test period, some providers accepted that opaque data across sessions or models where it should not have worked.
A weaker sibling model could reveal represented material, including secrets in public logs.
A purpose-built share file avoids releasing unreviewed backstage fields.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A coding assistant reads a deployment key, omits it from the final answer and leaves it represented in the raw technical session.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A travel assistant produces a shareable itinerary but its raw export may include connected-account continuity data.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Share a fresh allowlisted report or the checked final result, strip reasoning/signature/opaque fields from technical releases and rotate credentials if raw logs touched secrets while public.

analogyPlan.concept: Opaque continuity data must be bound to the right context.
analogyPlan.analogy: A sealed package is safe only when the receiving desk checks who sent it and where it belongs.
analogyPlan.mapping: Encryption seals the data; session/user/model binding controls where it may be accepted.
analogyPlan.limit: Provider cryptography and API protocols are more complex than a physical parcel and the article does not claim every sealed field is exposed.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It makes the difference between encryption and contextual authorization visible.

humourPlan.lessonJob: The backstage production-file line makes the safe share object memorable without making the leak funny.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Dated masthead; headline and standfirst; audience boundary; two-layer mechanism; study results and limits; mitigation status; workplace and non-work transfer; exact actions; LAiDIES read; cocktail-party summary; sources and correction trigger.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No forced headline correction, no API-first glossary, no cyber-thriller framing and no prompt offered as a security control.

explanationArc.adaptation: The Daily answers first, spends most space on mechanism and evidence, then lands without suspense.

explanationReasoningDesign.humanEntry: A smart non-technical reader wants to know whether private information can remain after she cleans what she sees.
explanationReasoningDesign.fakeUnderstandingRisk: She may panic about all chats, or assume a redacted screen proves the entire technical file is clean.
firstPrinciplesSequence: A visible answer and a raw technical session are different objects.
The raw session may include opaque continuity data.
Encryption does not authorize every session or model to reuse that data.
A new allowlisted share file limits release to inspected content.
explanationReasoningDesign.explainBackTest: Explain why removing a password from the visible chat does not prove a raw AI-session export is safe to publish.
explanationReasoningDesign.transferCase: A travel assistant's itinerary is safe to share only as the reviewed itinerary, not by assuming the connected-account session export contains nothing else.
explanationReasoningDesign.usefulLanding: Choose the object you intend to publish, construct it from approved fields and rotate secrets if a raw session may already have escaped.
explanationReasoningDesign.rewindEraAdaptation: Use backstage versus final cut once because it distinguishes the release artifact from production material; no decorative nostalgia.

evidenceAnalysis.claimUnderInspection: A new study means hidden AI reasoning is currently exposing ordinary users' private chats.
evidenceAnalysis.primaryEvidence: Panfilov et al. preprint plus current OpenAI, Anthropic and Google documentation on opaque reasoning or thought-state fields.
evidenceAnalysis.establishes: The authors reconstructed opaque reasoning data from public technical session records, found real secrets and demonstrated cross-context attacks during the tested period.
evidenceAnalysis.doesNotEstablish: A continuing exploit after disclosure, exposure caused by ordinary private chat use, leakage from every raw log or exact fidelity for every reconstructed token.
evidenceAnalysis.claimedImpact: All hidden AI reasoning is unsafe and users should ask the model to reveal it.
evidenceAnalysis.realConsequence: People who publish raw technical AI sessions must treat opaque fields as unreviewed data and release only approved fields; asking for reasoning is not a security check.
evidenceAnalysis.aidbReason: The scheduled August 12 AIDB/Mollick cycle did not cover the paper; Ali supplied a later private discovery lead, after which LAiDIES independently read the public primary evidence.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Repeating the rejected API-first explanation or turning a patched developer-log finding into a consumer-chat scare.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: A cold reader must identify who is affected, explain visible answer versus raw session, state the patched-status limit and choose the correct share object.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: Without using API or encrypted-reasoning jargon, the reader can explain why a cleaned chat is not necessarily a cleaned raw log and name the next action.
